children: Oil and gas producer Diamondback Energy signed a roughly $5 billion deal to beef up its presence in the Permian Basin, the largest crude field in the U.S.

The company, based in Midland, Texas, said on Monday that it is buying out the remaining interest in a development partnership formed with oil and gas company Double Eagle Energy. It said the deal consists of about 15.56 million shares of Diamondback stock and $2.15 billion of cash.
The transaction adds about 176,000 net acres and will augment Diamondback's production by 92,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day next year, it said.
Diamondback said the deal will allow it to drill more wells to tap into the Barnett Shale, a deep, promising layer of rock that it says is exceeding its expectations.

"Our confidence in both the quality of the resource and our execution cost structure ahead of large-scale development made this the right time to complete this transaction," said Diamondback CEO Kaes Van't Hof.
